implementation_notes: Ruby's standard library ships the decorator scaffold: SimpleDelegator takes the wrapped object in its constructor and forwards every supported call to it (with super reaching the wrapped implementation from an override), DelegateClass generates the same behaviour for a specific class, and Forwardable declares individual delegations when the public interface must stay explicit. That makes delegation the library-provided realization, and SimpleDelegator subclasses are the idiomatic object decorator in plain Ruby. Method-level decoration of a class or a single object is the other real option - prepend a module whose method calls super, or extend it onto one object - but it attaches behaviour to the class/singleton rather than to a wrapped instance, so it is a different trade-off (no second object, no per-instance composition choice).
idiom_name: SimpleDelegator subclass overriding selected methods with super (stdlib delegate); Forwardable for explicit per-method delegation
code_sketch:
require 'delegate'
class Milk < SimpleDelegator            # wrapper: forwards everything, overrides cost
  def cost
    super + 0.4                         # reaches the wrapped object's implementation
  end
end
class Sugar < SimpleDelegator           # the same shape composes: Sugar.new(Milk.new(2.0))
  def cost
    super + 0.2
  end
end
puts Sugar.new(Milk.new(2.0)).cost      # => 2.6
pitfalls: Delegator inherits from BasicObject, so Kernel methods (puts, class, is_a?) are not available inside the decorator, and forwarding everything also exposes methods you may not want to publish - use Forwardable/def_delegator when the public surface must stay explicit.

Identity changes: equality and hash are delegated, but case/when, is_a? and Rails-style type checks against the wrapped class fail, so code that branches on the concrete type behaves differently once decorated.

Delegator only forwards what the wrapped object responds to at call time; a typo or calling a method that existed on the component but not on the current delegate raises inside the wrapper, far from the call site.
